run.question:
The checkout-service in production-us-east-2 is throwing 500 errors right
now. Investigate the root cause using app-269-prod-logs.

report.summary: The question names production-us-east-2, and the only data that carries that cluster identity is the Elasticsearch index app-269-prod-logs (field cluster). In production-us-east-2 that index holds exactly 4 ERROR lines, all inside the authorized window, and they describe a fault chain: at 2026-11-22T08:17:51Z payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' while checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'; at 09:17:51Z checkout-service logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)'; at 09:47:51Z checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open' — the 500 symptom in the question. The deepest cause the evidence supports is therefore the us-east-2 payment provider dependency written in the evidence as stripe-us, which did not answer /v1/charges within 30s; payment-service's consequent failures tripped checkout-service's circuit breaker for payment-service, and checkout-service returned 500 without calling it. This is a supported reading of the error text, but it is partial: no telemetry from stripe-us itself, no traces or metrics (Jaeger and Prometheus both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE in this Run), and no Kubernetes access to production-us-east-2 (my cluster access reads only the cluster whose logs label themselves production-eu-west-2), so the reason stripe-us timed out and whether the 500s still continue after the last us-east-2 sample at 09:47:51Z are unknown. The two production-eu-west-2 log lines in the same index and the readable cluster's own workloads show no error — checkout there logged 'payment went through' repeatedly at 10:12–10:17Z and payment-service logged 'Adyen-eu healthy' — which is a different cluster and a different (Adyen-eu) provider and is not evidence of health in us-east-2.

claims.text: app-269-prod-logs contains, with cluster=production-us-east-2 and timestamp 2026-11-22T08:17:51Z, a checkout-service ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' and, at the same timestamp and cluster, a payment-service ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.

The same index contains a production-us-east-2 checkout-service ERROR at 2026-11-22T09:17:51Z reading 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)', and a second checkout-service ERROR at 2026-11-22T09:47:51Z reading 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open', which is the reported 500 on POST /api/checkout.

Across the full authorized window the index app-269-prod-logs matched exactly 6 documents: 4 with cluster=production-us-east-2 (level ERROR: 3 checkout-service, 1 payment-service) and 2 with cluster=production-eu-west-2 (level INFO: 1 checkout-service, 1 payment-service); the query's own time filter reported these as the only matches, with no document later than 2026-11-22T09:47:51Z.

The two production-eu-west-2 lines in the index are INFO and name a different provider and a healthy state: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 2026-11-22T08:17:51Z and payment-service 'Adyen-eu healthy' at 2026-11-22T09:47:51Z; they are labelled production-eu-west-2, not the cluster in the question.

The only Kubernetes cluster I can read is the one whose workloads are the otel-demo kind stack (33 pods, all phase Running and ready): there, pod otel-demo/checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' and 'order confirmation email sent' at 10:12:44Z, 10:13:44Z, 10:15:53Z, 10:16:56Z and 10:17:51Z with severity info, and the corresponding payment pod otel-demo/payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d is Ready with restartCount 2. This is a different cluster from production-us-east-2 and its logs identify themselves as production-eu-west-2.

Events in the readable cluster, grouped across all namespaces, are 9 in total: 6 Normal rollout events for namespace app-269 (Deployment checkout-service ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set checkout-service-6d7f474c45 from 0 to 1' at 2026-11-22T10:17:48Z, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-hrwfq Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started) and 3 Warning Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint in namespace default for mariadb (app-219), orca (app-95) and signup-service (app-162) at 09:21:00Z, 09:32:52Z and 10:07:47Z.

The app-269 checkout-service pod in the readable cluster runs image nginx:1.27-alpine and its only log lines are nginx startup notices from 2026-11-22T10:17:52Z onward ('ready for start up', 'start worker process ...'), so it does not emit the checkout-service application log lines seen in the index.

Likely cause chain for the production-us-east-2 checkout 500s: the payment provider written as stripe-us stopped answering payment-service's /v1/charges calls within 30s (08:17:51Z error text), payment-service's failure rate reached 41%, checkout-service's circuit breaker for payment-service opened (09:17:51Z), and checkout-service then failed POST /api/checkout immediately with 'circuit-breaker open' (09:47:51Z). The originating fault is the stripe-us dependency; payment-service's timeouts and checkout-service's open breaker are its propagation.

checkout-service's circuit-breaker threshold/settings in production-us-east-2 may be low enough that a 41% payment-service failure rate opens it quickly and keeps checkout returning 500 for longer than the upstream timeout itself; the settings were not readable (no ConfigMap access to production-us-east-2), so this is a candidate amplifier, not an established cause.

Rejected: that the 500s come from a checkout-service pod problem in namespace app-269 of the readable cluster. That pod runs nginx:1.27-alpine and logs only nginx startup notices from 10:17:52Z, its rollout events are Normal ScalingReplicaSet/SuccessfulCreate/Scheduled/Started at 10:17:48–10:17:51Z, and the production-us-east-2 application errors occur 30 to 90 minutes earlier; a startup readiness event on a fresh pod is not impact.

Rejected: that the 3 Warning Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint events (mariadb/app-219, orca/app-95, signup-service/app-162, namespace default) explain the checkout 500s. They concern other namespaces and services in the readable cluster (production-eu-west-2), while the failing checkout-service and payment-service log lines carry cluster=production-us-east-2 and name a payment-provider timeout, not an endpoint problem.

The healthy-looking eu-west-2 readings do not clear production-us-east-2: the two eu-west-2 lines are INFO and reference Adyen-eu, whereas the us-east-2 errors reference stripe-us; and the readable cluster's successful 'payment went through' checkout lines at 10:12–10:17Z belong to that other cluster's otel-demo checkout pod.

Verify the stripe-us payment provider's availability and the 30s charge timeout path for the us-east-2 payment-service (provider status page, provider incident history, then payment-service timeout/retry settings), since the evidence places the fault at that dependency rather than inside checkout-service.

Obtain read access to production-us-east-2 (pods, deployment status, events, ConfigMaps for checkout-service and payment-service) and to the Prometheus/Jaeger backends, so the payment-service error rate, checkout-service 500 rate and circuit-breaker settings can be measured rather than inferred from four log lines.

gaps: Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for traces_list_services and traces_search, so no spans (checkout-service operations, payment-service rpc calls, error status tags) exist for production-us-east-2 or stripe-us in this Run.

Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_all_labels and get_label_values, so no error-rate, latency or kube-state-metrics series (including any ERROR-count series) were readable; their values are unknown, not zero.

Kubernetes access reads only the cluster whose logs label themselves production-eu-west-2 (the otel-demo kind stack); there is no access to production-us-east-2 pods, deployments, ReplicaSets, events, ConfigMaps or resource state, so restart history, container termination reasons and any circuit-breaker/timeout configuration for the failing services are unchecked.
No logs or telemetry from the payment provider named stripe-us were observable, so why it stopped responding to /v1/charges within 30s is unknown.

The index app-269-prod-logs holds only 6 documents and the last production-us-east-2 sample is 2026-11-22T09:47:51Z, 30 minutes before the window end; whether checkout-service is still returning 500 at 2026-11-22T10:17:59Z cannot be confirmed from these logs.
Whether the two production-eu-west-2 log lines fully describe that cluster's state is unknown; they are two INFO lines only and no ERROR series or traces exist there to confirm health.
The change_history integration is not configured, so no deployment, configuration or provider change record could be checked for production-us-east-2.
next_steps: Ask the payment provider owner or status page whether stripe-us /v1/charges was degraded around 2026-11-22T08:00–09:50Z, and whether the 30s timeout is expected.

With access to production-us-east-2, inspect payment-service and checkout-service deployment status, pod restart counts and container last-termination reasons, and read their application logs for the period after 09:47:51Z.

Read checkout-service's circuit-breaker and payment-service's provider timeout/retry configuration in production-us-east-2 to see whether thresholds amplify a transient provider timeout into sustained 500s.
Once Grafana/Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable again, compare checkout-service 500 rate and payment-service error/latency series before 08:17:51Z as a baseline against the 08:17–09:47 period.
